display.title: Chodesh Elul: The King in the Field
display.summary_short: Why Elul makes us cry 'Oy gevald!': the Alter Rebbe's parable of the king who comes out to the fields, and the one request at the top of everyone's list.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, a few days before Rosh Chodesh Elul. Uncle Yossi says the very thought of Elul should send a chill down our spine, because something happens only in this month. Hashem is always close to the Jewish people, but the Alter Rebbe in Likkutei Torah gives a parable: a king usually sits in his guarded palace and can be reached only through ministers, but on his way home from a journey he passes through the fields, where everyone may come out to greet him; he is in a happy mood and grants every request. In Elul, before Rosh Hashanah, Hashem is like that king in the field, and every child, as a soldier in Tzivos Hashem, can approach Him. Of all our needs, the request at the top of the list is Moshiach, and like a loving father moved by his child's cry, Hashem will surely answer.
display.lesson: In Elul Hashem is especially close, so turn to Him and ask, above all, for Moshiach.
